lessons.claim: When looking at whether an integrator assumption (with or without inertia and so on) changes an observable, **a kT=0 deterministic difference** is overwhelmingly stronger than a thermal comparison. In chain-bend, Brownian vs Langevin (kT=1) could not exclude a difference below 47~51% at 3σ (the observed K″ difference was 18~19% -- no verdict possible), whereas OverdampedViscous vs Langevin (kT=0) had 0 statistical error and settled it at a maximum of **0.159%** across all 7 ω. ★ With no noise the SNR problem disappears, and since the two integrators share the same transient the common mode cancels. For a thermal comparison, compute the power first.
